currentEditorialSignals.title: Explain when a quiet trail is—and is not—better for dogs
currentEditorialSignals.signal: AllTrails and Komoot now use community heatmaps to help people choose popular routes or quieter alternatives. The underlying framing is about traffic and discovery, not dog-specific consequences.
currentEditorialSignals.ormaOpportunity: Develop an editorial and collection framework for “quieter with your dog” that separates human footfall from actual suitability. Explain that low traffic can reduce overstimulation but may coincide with livestock, guardian dogs, hunting activity, fewer witnesses, weak phone coverage, or poorly maintained paths. Link every recommendation back to reviewed route evidence.
currentEditorialSignals.whyNow: Quietness is becoming a mainstream route-selection attribute, creating room for ORMA to define the dog-first interpretation before users equate “less popular” with “safer.”
suggestedInvestigation: Which available datasets can estimate human traffic without overstating precision?
Which counter-signals—livestock, hunting, remoteness, access evidence—must accompany quietness?
Would users value a quietness filter, editorial collection, or both?
What wording prevents quiet routes being presented as universally preferable?
